title: Message Tailoring
description: The same argument persuades more when it is matched to the person hearing it.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: People accept a message more readily when it fits their values, their self-image and the way they already see the world. Tailoring the framing of a claim to the audience can matter more than the strength of the claim itself.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Matching a message reduces the sense of threat and increases perceived relevance. A message that already speaks the audience's language is easier to accept.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: A health message framed around responsibility persuades one group; the same advice framed around family persuades another.
A proposal emphasising efficiency lands with an operations lead; the identical proposal framed as growth lands with a founder.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: The argument reshaped to fit who is listening.
Language that mirrors the audience's own words.

sections.title: Ethical Uses
sections.content: Explaining the same true thing in terms that matter to the listener respects their perspective.

sections.title: Manipulative Uses
sections.content: Telling different audiences different things until the messages contradict each other.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: The same claim presented in incompatible ways to different groups.
Framing that flatters a bias rather than addressing it.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Ask what the argument looks like from another perspective.
Check whether the framing is doing more work than the facts.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Delivering one generic pitch to everyone.
Assuming a good argument works regardless of framing.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Framing is not decoration; it is the message.
Watch for messages that shift by audience.
